kept.reason: No assertion maps onto one_password_vault_store: this test checks the local copy (no op call while a token is valid, cross-machine sync without a second refresh, rebuild under a rotated service account token or a damaged copy, logout and archive reaching another machine); vault_store checks the vault wiring (item fields, no secret in files or argv). Setups conflict: this one's 30 s login token makes the first call refresh, while vault_store's refreshed-1 / --min-life assertions need an hour-long one, and its identity URL changes the op call/write counts asserted here.

Asserts the exact op calls a sync makes (list, which gets); the e2e test checks a refused write through a real op process and no call sequence (its doc defers that to these tests); the setups differ (in-memory Op vs a process), so they can't be merged

Asserts edit-vs-archive op calls and that another's field keeps the item from being archived; the e2e store test only checks the item is gone after reset+logout, through a process, so they can't be merged
Asserts one get per lock and a fresh read on the next lock; no e2e test asserts call counts, and the in-memory seam can't fold into a process-level test
A pure check of kept()/fields() on a literal item, no machine; nothing in an_item_left_empty_is_archived asserts kept()'s filtering, and with no shared setup a merge saves nothing

kept_files.reason: main.rs is the command-line seam: ~half its prod lines are the clap definitions and help text (the CLI's interface itself), the rest a dispatch where each arm is one call into a deep module (providers, oauth, source/refresh, standing, store, api::Call). Its 90-day churn is new flags/commands landing here and logic moving out (api.rs, standing.rs, source.rs, refresh.rs, wire.rs); the deletion test only moves the clap surface, it concentrates nothing. Left inline: a few lines of user messages and the stdin-or-prompt secret read used twice, too small to be a module.
